text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained to understand and generate human-like text. They work by analyzing vast amounts of written material, such as books, articles, and websites. Through this training data, they learn patterns and relationships between words. When you give one a prompt, it predicts the most likely next words to create a response. Prompt engineering is the skill of designing these input questions or requests clearly to get useful output. These models can write stories, answer questions, or translate languages, but they have limits. They sometimes make mistakes or invent facts. They do not truly understand meaning; instead, they mimic patterns. Also, their knowledge is based only on their training, which may become outdated. So, while powerful, LLMs should be used wisely, with human oversight.
